intended_object: The canonical group isomorphism between the column group C(t) of a Young tableau t of shape μ (the permutations of the labels that keep every label in its column) and the product over the columns j of μ of the symmetric groups Sym(column j), i.e. C(t) ≅ ∏_j S_{col_j}. Taken from the docstring and Fulton, Young Tableaux §7.1.
explanation:
The definition is a composite of three maps. First, `MulEquiv.subgroupCongr` identifies `colSubgroup t` with the subgroup `fiberSubgroup (colIndex t)` of permutations that preserve the fibers of the column-index map. Second, the library's `fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm` sends a fiber-preserving permutation to the family of its restrictions to the fibers; it is built from Mathlib's `DomMulAct.stabilizerMulEquiv`. Third, each fiber {k | colIndex t k = j} is carried to the cells of column j of μ (`μ.col j`) by `colFiberEquiv`, which applies `t.symm`. These conjugations go through `permCongrHom` and `MulEquiv.piCongrRight`.

The result is the standard isomorphism C(t) ≅ ∏_j Sym(column j). Its j-th component sends the cell holding label k to the cell holding label σ k, as the companion lemma `colSubgroupMulEquiv_apply_coe` confirms. Columns j at or beyond the length of the first row are empty and give trivial factors, so indexing by all j : ℕ does no harm.

The general construction (fiber-preserving permutations ≅ product of the permutation groups of the fibers) already lives in the library's `fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm` and in Mathlib's `DomMulAct.stabilizerMulEquiv`. This definition only specialises it to Young-tableau columns, which is the whole content of the notion. So it is not too narrow, and it is faithful.
